title: Resting-state EEG before and after different study methods
description: Open-access resting-state EEG recordings from 21 neurotypical undergraduate students at the Federal University of Paraíba, Brazil, collected before and after different study methods. Participants were randomly assigned to an active learning group (retrieval practice with feedback), a passive learning group (review of lecture notes), or a control group with no review. The dataset supports research in cognitive neuroscience, educational neuroscience, and the neural correlates of learning and memory.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel ActiChamp system (Brain Products) using active Ag/AgCl electrodes placed according to the 10-20 system. Impedance was kept below 15 kΩ, the ground was at Fpz, and the sampling rate was 500 Hz with 0.5-50 Hz filtering. Each of two sessions (pre- and post-intervention) lasted about nine minutes and comprised two eyes-open and two eyes-closed blocks of 2 min 15 s each. Data are organized in BIDS format as BrainVision files.
